hints.text: Rewrite the log in exponential form. The base stays the base, and the answer becomes the exponent.
In exponential form, $\log_4(x) = 3$ means $4^3 = x$. Work out the product $4 \times 4 \times 4$ to find $x$.
Since $4^3 = 64$, the solution of the equation is $x = 64$.

explanation: A log equation can always be rewritten as an exponential equation that says the same thing.
The statement $\log_4(x) = 3$ says that $4$ raised to the power $3$ gives $x$.
Computing the power, $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$, shows that the solution is $x = 64$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it as a sentence
steps: Say it out loud: "$4$ to WHAT power is $x$? The answer is $3$."
So $x$ must be $4$ multiplied by itself $3$ times.

alternativeExplanations.title: Undo with a power
steps: Logs and exponents are undo twins.
The left side collapses to $x$, so $x = 64$.
